title: Bounding Related-Key Differential Characteristic Weights
summary: Techniques cover different numbers of rounds at no weight cost, leaving open how to upper-bound chosen related-key differential characteristic weights and prove attack resistance.

formal_statement.body: Develop a sound method to estimate upper bounds on the weights of chosen related-key differential characteristics and use those bounds to prove resistance to chosen related-key differential attacks. The method must account for techniques that cover different numbers of rounds without weight cost: one round for the rebound attack, two rounds for the Super-Sbox technique, and still more rounds for the tool of Khovratovich and collaborators.

scope.domain: Chosen related-key differential cryptanalysis of byte-oriented block ciphers.
parameters: Characteristic weight—the quantity whose upper bound is needed to prove resistance
Free-round count—the number of rounds an attack technique covers without weight cost
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a sound upper-bound method that accounts for technique-dependent free-round coverage and use it to prove resistance to chosen related-key differential attacks.

citations.label: Automatic Search for Related-Key Differential Characteristics in Byte-Oriented Block Ciphers: Application to AES, Camellia, Khazad and Others

progress.summary: The source explicitly labels proving resistance as open, attributing the obstacle to the lack of a sound weight bound when different techniques cover different numbers of rounds for free.
